blogs.title: Automate medical coding with Step Functions and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
blogs.summary: Learn how to combine deterministic orchestration with bounded agentic reasoning using AWS Step Functions and the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness. This medical coding workflow escalates cheapest-first: a safety block-list, then exact matching, then an AI agent only for terms that need judgment, keeping every routing decision auditable.

Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
blogs.summary: Naive byte-range caching can waste gigabytes of origin bandwidth on small requests. We rebuilt our cache architecture in Pingora to coordinate partial fetches automatically, cutting R2 p99 latency in half.

blogs.title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
blogs.summary: Cloudflare's new post-quantum GeoKey Manager protects geographically fenced decryption keys from harvest now, decrypt later attacks. Learn how we redesigned our cryptography stack to support strict data sovereignty in a post-quantum world.

blogs.title: Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
blogs.summary: Cloudflare has achieved South Korea's ISMS certification following an audit across 80 controls. Learn how we localized user consent flows, adapted social sign-up paths at the edge, and validated our global security program.

blogs.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
blogs.summary: Cloudflare's web application firewall can now correlate an HTTP request with its response. Full transaction detection helps every customer find successful exploits, data exposure, and risky misconfigurations that request-only inspection can miss.

blogs.title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
blogs.summary: Cloudflare has deployed default web application firewall (WAF) protections for newly disclosed PHP vulnerabilities before public disclosure. The rules use request and response signals to stop exploit attempts and prevent exposed data from reaching attackers.

blogs.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
blogs.summary: Almost 100,000 Commerce.com domains now give AI agents real shopping tools through WebMCP on Cloudflare. Here's how we turned it on across every store at once, while keeping each merchant in control.

blogs.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
blogs.summary: Following the discovery that eight eMudhra intermediate certificates use weak keys, Cloudflare is deploying mitigations and releasing client updates. We explain the impact, our response, and what customers and developers should do next.

blogs.title: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
blogs.summary: Cloudflare is collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that is up to 8x faster and uses 70% less memory.

blogs.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
blogs.summary: When our AI code reviewer's cost per run doubled, we dug into the token usage to find out why. Learn how we used prompt caching and intelligent model routing to slash our inference bill by 68% while speeding up reviews.

blogs.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
blogs.summary: Clairic is a new model from Cloudflare that is a System One extraction modeI, capable of extracting, computing, estimating, and forecasting data from unstructured inputs.

blogs.title: Article: The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code
blogs.summary: Agentic LLM systems have moved from linear prompt chains to graph-based workflows and, more recently, code-executing harnesses. Chains are simple but fragile, graphs add branching, retries, and validation, and code harnesses verify outputs through execution. The article advises validating model outputs and choosing the least complex design that meets reliability, speed, and cost needs. By Karthik …

blogs.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
blogs.summary: Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

blogs.title: PHP Patches Two Critical RCE Flaws That Were Already Under Attack
blogs.summary: PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 to fix two critical vulnerabilities allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Amazon recorded an exploitation attempt four days before the patches shipped, and operators spent the day working out whether they ran PHP, where to get the package, and how to tell it had landed. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

blogs.title: PingCAP Breach Exposes Customer Records and Source Code
blogs.summary: PingCAP recently confirmed unauthorized access to its internal systems and the theft of source code and customer-related data. The attacker, cyber extortion group FulcrumSec, claimed to have stolen 10.6 TB of data, including TiDB Cloud control-plane records, customer SQL statements, API keys, connection logs, billing information, internal documents, and 413 private source-code repositories. By Ren…

blogs.title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
blogs.summary: Google has made Data Agent Kit generally available, a free set of MCP tools and 37 open-source skills that connect coding agents to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services. Two kinds of guardrail ship with it, and practitioners need to tell them apart: one is a skill asking the agent to stop, the other an IAM deny policy that refuses the call. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

blogs.title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
blogs.summary: Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90%. By Renato Losio

blogs.title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS
blogs.summary: CSIRO has developed Serverless Beacon, a serverless architecture for querying genomic variants without copying VCF files into a central database. The system combines Amazon S3, Lambda, Athena and DynamoDB, using metadata indexes and HTTP byte range requests to query compressed genomic regions. Tests reported 1.52 second average latency for 10,000 base pair queries. By Leela Kumili

blogs.title: AWS Introduces Lambda Web Functions for Node.js Applications
blogs.summary: AWS recently introduced Lambda Web Functions, allowing developers to run Node.js web applications using frameworks such as Express and Hono directly on Lambda, with support for concurrent requests and response streaming. By Renato Losio

blogs.title: Article: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
blogs.summary: Multi-cloud flexibility comes with hidden egress costs driven by service placement and communication patterns. This article applies Backend FinOps to cross-cloud architecture, covering cost visibility through FOCUS, workload placement, synchronization models, and CI/CD-integrated cost governance. A controlled experiment shows architecture changes saved far more than rate negotiation alone. By Vive…

blogs.title: Presentation: Move Fast, Don’t Break Trust: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond
blogs.summary: Suhail Patel discusses how Monzo structures its software engineering organization and technical stack to ship safely hundreds of times a day. He shares insights into opinionated microservice abstractions, tenancy-based staging, static analysis checks, continuous profiling, demonstrating how a strong internal platform enables engineers and LLMs to iterate rapidly without sacrificing reliability. By…

blogs.title: Study Finds AI-generated Code Fails to Boost Productivity Due to Downstream Bottlenecks
blogs.summary: A recent Harvard study of 718 firms, using the Jellyfish analytics platform, finds that although AI coding assistants and agents increase code volume, this does not translate into a corresponding increase in completed work, partly because AI-generated code increases the workload in later stages of development, particularly code review. By Sergio De Simone

blogs.title: Presentation: Actors for Agents: Patterns for Production AI
blogs.summary: Manju Rajashekhar explains how the actor model solves the complex runtime challenges of production AI agents. By treating agents as distributed systems, he discusses state ownership, message passing, write-through state, and supervision boundaries to manage failures, continuations, and mutable execution graphs, moving agentic workflows beyond fragile demos to resilient architecture. By Manju Rajas…

blogs.title: Article: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
blogs.summary: This article presents a disaster-recovery analytics workflow in which an AI agent generates constrained SQL or Python, DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet, and the agent interprets the results. It explains the determinism split, replayable analysis, and four signals for deciding when an embedded engine is sufficient or a managed lakehouse is justified. By Peihao Yuan

blogs.title: Developer behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready"
blogs.summary: A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

blogs.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
blogs.summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS.…
